newsitem.title: FRANCE: GE will not build Airbus A340-600.
newsitem.headline: GE will not build Airbus A340-600.

text.p: General Electric Aircraft Engines, a unit of U.S. General Electric Co, will not build the GEXX engines for Airbus's planned stretched versions of its A340 plane, Airbus confirmed on Tuesday.
Newspaper La Tribune said that after 10 months of exclusive talks, Airbus Industrie and GE were unable to conclude a deal due to differences over pricing and risk sharing.

"We were unable to agree business terms and conditions," an Airbus spokesman told Reuters. The report said GE was unwilling to take a too-large share in the project and its prices and commercial concessions failed to win Airbus approval.
French aero engine company Snecma SNC.CN has said it was ready to take a 25 percent share in the GEXX project, which would power the stretched A340-500 and A340-600 versions of the long haul jet.
"We are actively evaluating alternative solutions," said the Airbus spokesman, declining further comment.
Rolls-Royce Plc and Pratt & Whitney, a United Technologies subsidiary, are the only two other companies making large engines.
Airbus is still aiming to put the A340-600 into service in 2001, the spokesman said.
Airbus needs the A340 derivatives to compete against Boeing's monopoly of the large capacity segment.
The A340-600 would seat 375 passengers in three classes compared 295 for the current A340-300 version.
